chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: Chattanooga Choo Choo and Capitol's offer for the contract
summary: After a second Rendezvous session, Capitol offers to buy the contract; Fields holds out for fifty thousand and ends up signing without payment.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Then I'm in Rendezvous now and so when I did the second session, it went going very good, and after this had gone so good, we decided and talked it over, let's do something else that Glenn Miller had had going good, because we saw that that was (inaudible). So we did Chattanooga Choo Choo and so then Capitol began to take notice and so Capitol contacted me and wanted to buy the contract, they wanted to buy my contract.

So they got on Rod and said how can you get a hold of Ernie Fields and so Rod told them and so I said Rod, what do you say? He said yeah, if they give us enough money, if I sell that I'm going to sell you too, I think we ought to get fifty thousand. He said we'll have twenty five a piece; and so I said okay and that's what I said to Capitol.
So they wouldn't go for it and they offered me twenty five and I wouldn't take that because like Rod said, but I kind of wish I would have gone on in, but didn't. I wouldn't go against him.
I kind of had a little malice because that twenty five would have meant so much to me and I thought that he should--
Did Rod go along with it?

When my contract was out I went to Capitol and so naturally when I went, what had made it possible, all of us, I talked to Rene Players and all of them and they said yeah, we're with you all the way. You came in there and suggested and your name is what made Capitol want it, so we'll all go on to Capitol.
So we went over to Capitol but not paying a dime for me.

No.
I'm angry because (inaudible),
you might say a little lousy session and maybe
two or three hundred bucks; that's it, you know,
when I did the session.
